title: The Night Watch
hook: Its famous name is a mistake.
caption:
Its famous name is a mistake. 🌙❌

Rembrandt never called it the Night Watch. The name first shows up in 1797, after layers of darkened varnish had buried his light. Then look closer: a glowing girl who is really a logo, an eye under a beret that may be Rembrandt himself, and three figures sliced off in 1715 so it would fit a wall. It survived knives, acid and a war spent rolled up in a cave.

Swipe for the secrets, then watch the reel and step inside the painting. Save this for your next trip to Amsterdam.

notes: Cover hook teases the misnomer; slide 3 pays it off (name first recorded 1797, varnish cleaned in the 1940s). Day-vs-night kept hedged ('brought the light back'), since the Rijksmuseum director has said only that it is not certain it is a night scene. Self-portrait is hedged ('historians think it may be'). Slide 9's ring marks the hand's shadow on the lieutenant's coat, placed by eye. The lost-strip line on slide 7 is drawn at about 11% of the copy's width (64.4 cm of about 525 cm), so it is approximate. CTA phone uses assets/nightwatch/nightwatch_first_frame_ai.png.
